bull_argument.argument:
Meta is a 26% revenue grower (64.601B vs 51.242B in the comparable quarter) trading at a provider-reported forward P/E of 17.14 after a 21.8% drawdown from the 52-week high. The reported Q3 operating margin of 20.1% is distorted by a 9.89B legal charge (web, release coverage); excluding it the margin is about 35% (inference), still an ad franchise with 79.3% gross margin. Management's Q4 revenue guide of 73-76B (web) implies growth of roughly 22-27% against Q4 2025's 59.893B, so the top line shows no demand break.

The tape has moved far ahead of the fundamentals. RSI-14 of 23.9 is deeply oversold, price is 15.1% lower over 20 bars, and the last bar (2026-11-06) closed above the prior close on volume 0.62x average after a 583.80 intraday low on 2026-11-05. Part of the move is a sector de-leveraging event (Nasdaq reportedly down about 5.5% on 2026-11-05) rather than Meta-specific news, and sell-side counts remain 55 buy-type ratings out of 62.
key_points: Revenue +26.1% YoY with Q4 guide implying roughly +22-27%
Forward P/E 17.14 and price 21.8% below 52-week high
Ex-legal operating margin about 35% (inference) shows the core franchise intact
RSI 23.9 oversold; last bar held above prior close on light volume
Sell-off partly sector-wide de-leveraging, not Meta-specific

bear_argument.argument:
The bull case leans on adjusted figures. On the reported basis, operating margin is 20.1% versus 40.1% a year ago, free cash flow is -1.157B versus +11.17B, and total debt is 114.84B versus 51.06B. Legal charges have now hit two consecutive quarters (about 2.4B in Q2 per the prior run, 9.89B in Q3), so adding them back assumes a recurrence of zero that nobody has shown. Even on the bull's own ex-charge figure of about 35%, margin is still roughly 4.7 points below last year while expenses are guided to 175-179B and capex to 135-145B for 2026 (web).

The 17.14x forward multiple depends on consensus estimates absent from the evidence, and cash balances, 2027 spending and financing plans are all unknown; a new nonvoting share class was announced with no financing plan (web). Price sits below SMA-20, SMA-50 and SMA-200 with a negative and widening MACD histogram (-5.89), and the macro desk finds a 10-2 Fed hold with two dissents for a hike and a December hike reportedly mostly priced (secondary sources). An oversold RSI in a downtrend is not a floor.
key_points: Reported op margin 20.1% vs 40.1% a year ago; ex-charge margin still lower
FCF -1.157B and total debt more than doubled YoY to 114.84B
Legal charges in consecutive quarters; add-back assumes no recurrence
Below all three moving averages, MACD histogram -5.89 and falling
Hawkish rate path and AI-capex risk-off; cash, 2027 outlook and financing unknown
bear_argument.rebuttal_to_previous: The ex-charge margin of 35% is an inference from a web-sourced charge size, not a reported figure, and it still shows compression; the forward P/E rests on unseen estimates; and RSI oversold is a context flag, not a trend change, while the last bar's +0.8% on light volume is too weak to call exhaustion.

bull_argument.argument:
Conceding the bear's points on legal recurrence and the unseen estimates, the question is what price already embeds. At 610.15 the market has taken the stock from 762.50 (2026-10-13) to 605.08 (2026-11-05) in about three weeks, with 51.3M and 40.6M volume capitulation-style sessions, while the revenue guide for Q4 (73-76B, web) and Q3 growth of 26% were not cut. The reported margin collapse is dominated by one identifiable charge, and the sequential debt increase from 112.32B to 114.84B in Q3 was only 2.3%, so the balance-sheet step-up happened mostly in Q2.

Negative free cash flow of -1.157B on about 35B of quarterly capex is a choice about investment timing, not an operating loss: operating cash flow was reportedly 32.8B (web). Price is 3.3% below SMA-200 and 17.5% above the 52-week low, so it is not in free fall relative to its own year. A debt-funded build-out is a risk, but the forward multiple already discounts it.
key_points: Price already fell about 20% in three weeks without a cut to growth guidance
Q3 debt rose only 2.3% sequentially; the step-up occurred in Q2
Operating cash flow reportedly 32.8B; negative FCF reflects capex timing
Only 3.3% below SMA-200 and 17.5% above the 52-week low
bull_argument.rebuttal_to_previous: The bear cites a hawkish Fed and risk-off tape, but those are market-wide and already reflected in a 21.8% drawdown; legal charges are lumpy, and the bear provides no evidence of a third charge. The bear's unknowns (cash, estimates) cut both ways, so they are not evidence of weakness.

bear_argument.argument:
The bull's reply that the price already discounts the risks is an assertion, not evidence: the forward multiple is a provider number on estimates not in the evidence set, and the price series shows the stock still 3.3% below its 200-day average with momentum still negative. Operating cash flow of 32.8B is web-sourced and management's own FCF is -2.12B after leases; calling that 'timing' presumes returns on capex that Q3 did not demonstrate, and 2027 capex has no guidance (web). The sequential debt change is small, but the level (114.84B) is already about 2.25x last year's and the cash side is blank, so net leverage cannot be bounded.

The bull's capitulation reading is also unproven: the last bar's volume was only 0.62x average and the 2026-11-05 low of 583.80 is only 4.3% under the close, well above the 524.08 and 519.37 prior lows. Rates add a second headwind: if the December hike is delivered while financing needs rise, the discount rate rises just as free cash flow is negative. The honest position is that a falling knife with unresolved funding questions is not yet a buy.
key_points: 'Already priced in' is asserted; forward multiple depends on unseen estimates
Management FCF is -2.12B (web) and 2027 capex is unguided
Debt level 2.25x year ago; cash balance unknown so net leverage unbounded
Capitulation unproven: last-bar volume 0.62x average, momentum still negative
Rate path adds a discount-rate headwind while FCF is negative
bear_argument.rebuttal_to_previous: The bull's strongest new point is that debt rose only 2.3% sequentially, but the level and the missing cash figure matter more than the quarterly delta. The 20% fall is price, not evidence about cash returns on capex, and a 3.3% distance below SMA-200 does not show a bottom.

bull_case_summary: A 26% grower with a roughly 35% ex-charge operating margin (inference) trades at a forward P/E of 17.14 after a roughly 20% fall in three weeks, with RSI 23.9, unchanged growth guidance for Q4 and a sector-wide de-leveraging that is not Meta-specific.
bear_case_summary: Reported margin halved, free cash flow is negative, debt has more than doubled year over year, legal charges recur, cash and 2027 capex are unknown, the trend is below all averages with weakening MACD, and a hawkish rate path raises the hurdle for debt-funded AI spending.
key_points_of_agreement: Revenue growth of 26.1% year over year is strong and not in dispute
Reported free cash flow is negative (-1.157B provider basis) and debt is much higher than a year ago
RSI-14 of 23.9 is oversold and price is below SMA-20, SMA-50 and SMA-200
A large legal charge distorted Q3 operating income and legal charges are not shown to be finished
key_points_of_disagreement: Whether ex-charge margin of about 35% is the right earnings base or whether recurring legal costs make 20.1% closer to reality
Whether the 21.8% drawdown and 17.14x forward P/E already discount the capex and rate risks
Whether negative FCF is capex timing or evidence of weak returns on investment
Whether oversold RSI and light-volume last bar signal exhaustion or a continuing downtrend
unresolved_uncertainties: Cash and securities balance at 2026-09-30 and therefore net debt (not in the evidence set)
2027 capex, expense and revenue outlook (management gave none, per web)
Financing intentions behind the new nonvoting share class
Consensus estimates behind the forward P/E and analyst reaction to Q3 (no dated post-Q3 target changes found)
Fed path: October CPI and the December decision; probabilities come from conflicting secondary sources
